You'll know, Every time. Book a Demo Start Free Trial More Than a Dashboard. It Tells You What the Data Means. PractiTest’s Release Readiness Index does more than report coverage, execution, and defect risk. It interprets those signals together through a built-in opinionated quality model, weighs what matters most as the project progresses, and turns them into one evolving readiness score. One score. Three quality signals. Instead of reading reports, jumping between dashboards, and stitching together spreadsheets you can instantly see where the release stands, what’s missing, where the risk is, and what needs attention next. Coverage Confidence See whether your release scope is sufficiently covered and identify coverage gaps that still need attention. Execution Confidence Understand whether testing is progressing as expected and where execution needs more focus as the release approaches. Remaining Defect Risk Identify where unresolved defects are creating risk and understand their potential impact on the release. From Release Scope to Release Readiness 1 2 3 4 5 Step 01 · Scope Define the release scope Create a PractiTest Milestone for the release, or sync a Jira sprint to automatically bring its scope into PractiTest and keep changes aligned. Step 02 · Coverage Build Coverage Confidence Connect existing tests to the requirements in scope, create new tests where needed, and identify coverage gaps and edge cases that still need attention. Step 03 · Execution Build Execution Confidence Execute your tests, track progress as results come in, and keep prioritizing what matters most as the release moves forward. Step 04 · Defects Reduce Remaining Defect Risk See which unresolved defects still carry risk and how their priority affects readiness, so you can focus on what matters most. Step 05 · Decision Bring Readiness Into the Release Conversation Bring a current view of release confidence, remaining risk, and what needs attention next into stakeholder conversations. This allows us to analyze our comprehensive results before we release them to production. Siva Kopparapu, Director of Technology, PartsSource Thanks to PractiTest, we have a unified approach to testing for multiple delivery units in our organization. The Testing Center of Excellence has gained recognition and appreciation. Mohita Parsad, AST (acquired by IBM) The flexible filtering system is a standout feature. It allows us to slice and dice data to focus on what’s most important- whether by product, model or team” Akhil G, Senior Test Manager We evaluated several different test management platforms and chose PractiTest as our company standard. We are now consolidating our various test management systems into PractiTest. Arthur Meloy, VP Site Reliability Engineering at NCR FAQ 1. What is the Release Readiness Index? The Release Readiness Index is PractiTest’s opinionated readiness model for active Milestones. It combines requirement coverage, test execution, and remaining defect risk to help teams understand where a release stands and what is influencing its readiness. 2. How is the Release Readiness Index calculated? The index combines three signals: Coverage Confidence, Execution Confidence, and Remaining Defect Risk. How those signals contribute to the overall score dynamically adjusts based on your progress through the Milestone, so the score reflects the current stage of the release. 3. How is the Release Readiness Index different from a dashboard? A dashboard brings testing metrics into one view, but the interpretation is still left to the team. The Release Readiness Index applies a dedicated, opinionated model to those signals and produces one readiness score that reflects both your testing data and where you are in the Milestone. 4. Does the Release Readiness Index update during the release? Yes. The index updates continuously throughout an active Milestone and dynamically adjusts based on your progress through it, so the readiness score reflects the current stage of the release and the signals that matter most at that point. 5. Do I need Jira to use Release Readiness? No. Release Readiness works with PractiTest Milestones. Jira Sprint Sync provides an additional workflow for Jira teams by automatically bringing sprint scope into PractiTest and keeping it aligned. 6. Can I see what is driving the readiness score? Yes. Each of the three signals has its own score, so you can see what is pulling overall readiness up or down. For example, if requirements in the Milestone lack sufficient test coverage, Coverage Confidence will be lower, making it clear where the readiness score is being affected and what needs attention. 7.

jobs.description: SmartFox AI Assistant Skip to content Get a Demo Product Release readiness index integrations Pricing Resources Resources Hub Customers Test Management Comparison Quality Leadership Academy Help Product Release readiness index integrations Pricing Resources Resources Hub Customers Test Management Comparison Quality Leadership Academy Help Product integrations Resources Customers Pricing Help Login US Data Center EU Data Center AU Data Center Product integrations Resources Customers Pricing Help Login US Data Center EU Data Center AU Data Center Log In US Data Center EU Data Center AU Data Center Log In US Data Center EU Data Center AU Data Center Talk To Us Get a Demo << Back to all articles SmartFox AI Assistant Help >> Test Planning and Execution >> SmartFox AI Assistant Getting Started Test Planning and Execution Data Management and Analysis Integration Options Automation Integration Settings and Customization General Actions API discussion forums SmartFox is PractiTest’s built-in AI assistant designed to help you save valuable time and simplify the manual test creation process, which is often one of the most labor-intensive parts of test management. SmartFox helps reduce the manual effort by providing intelligent, AI-generated test steps, based on the test data. Note: In order to use the SmartFox, please ensure that your account owner has accepted the beta terms of use and enabled this feature in the account settings . Generating New Test Steps If your test does not yet contain any steps and you’d like to quickly generate relevant ones, start by giving your test a clear name and a comprehensive description. Based on this input, SmartFox will generate well-defined and relevant steps. How to Use Fill in the Title and Description fields of your test. Navigate to the Steps tab. Click the ‘ Step Generator ’ button. A pop-up window will appear, showing that SmartFox is working on generating steps. Within a few moments, SmartFox will begin presenting multiple-step suggestions, one by one, for your review. Once SmartFox have done generating steps, you’ll see the full list of steps on the screen. To add them to your tests, please click ‘ Apply Steps ‘ at the bottom right corner. After clicking the ‘ Apply Steps ’ button, you’ll return to the test where the selected steps will be added. Please make sure to click the Save button to save the steps. Refining SmartFox Generated Steps Once SmartFox has generated your initial test steps, you can fine-tune them to better suit your needs.At the bottom of the pop-up window, you’ll find a text box where you can enter instructions for how you’d like SmartFox to improve the steps. This is especially useful if you want the steps to be more concise or detailed. Some examples can be: “Shorten the steps”, “Elaborate the steps with more context”, or “Add more steps”. Using the Step Generator with Existing Steps You can also use SmartFox’s Step Generator to refine and improve tests that already have defined steps. Open a test that has existing steps. Click the Step Generator button. The SmartFox Step Generator screen will open, displaying the current steps. Click the arrow next to the Apply Steps button to open two action options: Replace Steps – SmartFox will generate a completely new set of steps, replacing your existing ones. Add as New Steps – SmartFox will generate additional steps and append them after your existing steps. Once you’ve selected your preferred option, the new steps will appear in the test. Click Save to finalize and apply the changes. Text Enhance The Text Enhance capability, powered by SmartFox AI, helps you instantly refine, shorten, or elaborate text within your test fields. This feature is available for the following fields: Description Preconditions Step Description Expected Results How It Works Next to each supported field, you’ll see an “Enhance with AI” icon. Clicking this icon opens an inline suggestion panel displaying AI-generated improvements for your text. You can choose one of the following enhancement options: Refine Text – Rephrases the text for better clarity and flow. Shorten – Shorten the text while keeping its meaning. Elaborate – Expands the text with more context or detail. Reviewing and Applying Suggestions Once the AI suggestions are generated, you have the ability to select whether to apply it or not. In any case, the new AI suggestions are not applied automatically. After reviewing the suggestions, you can: Accept Changes – Apply the AI suggestion. You can then choose to either: Insert – Add the new text alongside the existing one. Replace – Overwrite the existing text with the enhanced version. Reject Changes – Keep the original text with no modifications. Interactive Refinement After the initial AI enhancement, you can further refine the generated text by providing additional feedback. This includes: Input Text + Send Button – Type specific instructions for SmartFox (e.g., “make it more concise” or “add an example”) and click the Send button to generate a refined version. Back and Forth Buttons – Navigate between previous and next enhancement versions to review and compare different outputs. About PractiTest A leader in the test management tool market, PractiTest is a SaaS end-to-end QA management system with some of the most advanced and interesting features. With PractiTest, testers and test managers are able to focus on quality and their actual work rather than side tasks. About PractiTest Security In PractiTest, we understand the importance of security, privacy, and the reliability of information. Our platform was designed to make sure only you and your users can access your information, and we work with the best practices and top partners (such as E&Y for SOC, AWS, etc) in the business to make sure our system is always secure, available, and accessible from anywhere in the world. PractiTest is and always was a SaaS only platform; as such, PT was designed and built from the beginning with all the security considerations in mind. Over the years, as our client base grew, we kept adding layers to make our system even more secure. Some of the practices that we have today are listed below. For the full SOC-II type 2 report, please contact us. Security layers From the ground to the top, we see our security as layer by layer: Layer 1 - Physical Security & Access PractiTest is hosted in AWS US, EU and AU data centers. AWS provides physical data center access only to approved employees and authorized third parties. Access requests are granted based on the principle of least privilege, meaning access will be limited to the layer of the data center the individual needs access to and will be time-bound. To read more about this, please visit the AWS data center . Layer 2 - Infrastructure Services vcp Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) lets us launch AWS resources into a virtual network that we defined. This virtual network closely resembles a traditional network that you’d operate in your own data center, with the benefits of using the scalable infrastructure of AWS. This means complete control over our virtual networking environment. We also use VPC features, such as Security Groups, to control network access between different resources (load balancers and machines, for example). Security Groups Security groups act as a firewall for associated Amazon EC2 instances, controlling both inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. For each security group, we have designated rules that control the inbound traffic to instances, and a separate set of rules that control the outbound traffic. RDS We use Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) to set up, operate, and scale our relational database. It provides us with resizable capacity while automating time-consuming administration tasks such as hardware provisioning, database setup, patching, and backups. It frees us to focus on the PractiTest application, so we can give our clients the fast performance, high availability, security, and compatibility they need. We use RDS security best practices: encryption and network isolation (inside a VPC). In addition, all of our production environment databases are deployed in multiple availability zones to provide enhanced durability and high availability. AWS Identity & Access Management Manage User Access to AWS services and resources. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) ensures that access to AWS services and resources is always secured. PoLP configuration (Principle of Least Privilege) The principle of least privilege is the practice of limiting access rights for users to the bare minimum permissions they need to perform their work. It is applied to restrict access rights for applications, systems, processes, and devices to only those permissions required to perform authorized activities. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) MFA is an authentication method that requires more than one piece of evidence to verify a user’s identity before login. We use MFA only to log in to our AWS console. AWS Certificate Manager - Provision, Manage, and Deploy SSL/TLS Certificates With AWS Certificate Manager, PractiTest can provision, manage, and deploy public and private Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS) certificates. SSL/TLS certificates are used to secure network communications and establish the identity of websites over the Internet as well as resources on private networks. AWS CloudTrail - User activity and API usage Tracking AWS CloudTrail is a service that enables governance, compliance, operational auditing, and risk auditing for our AWS account. With CloudTrail, we continuously monitor and retain account activity related to actions across the AWS infrastructure. CloudTrail provides event history of PractiTest’s AWS account activity, including actions taken through the AWS Management Console, AWS SDKs, command line tools, and other AWS services.
